title: Changing to the POV-Ray Display_Gamma from 2.2 to match the default sRGB standard
body:
This change will make POV-Ray use the sRGB gamma curve instead of simple power of 2.2. Since sRGB is the de facto standard on the internet, this should be the default for dissemination. The current value of 2.2 is nearly identical but there may be some small improvements from switching to the sRGB gamma curve. This might be pedantic at the moment, but could give some future proofing. 

more info: https://wiki.povray.org/content/User:Clipka/Gamma#Perceptual_Brightness_and_Gamma_Encoding
author: mjwaters

comments.author: mjwaters
comments.body:
Hi @yuzie007, 

In 2022, I was trying to design a color palette to enforce good elemental contrast for a publication.[1] I noticed that the POV-Ray rendering colors were far from what I selected. From this, I found that we needed to be setting display_gamma=2.2 to match the sRGB standard[2] for image files would have the correct colors. Unfortunately, making this change drastically changed the appearance of the default styles (e.g. 'ase3', 'simple', 'glass', ...). So I tried to faithfully recreate them with the updated display_gamma.[3] At the time, I was more concerned about backwards compatibility and getting the MR completed (so I could have correct colors) than I was about the minute differences between a gamma=2.2 curve and the sRGB standard.[4] As a bonus, the ASE website's images immediately looked much more colorful.[5]

Now that 4 years have past, I thought it would be worth investigating oldest version of POV-Ray that I could confirm supported the exact sRGB gamma curve with the display_gamma=sRGB tag. After seeing that 3.7, which supports display_gamma=sRGB, was released 13 years ago, I didn't bother looking back any farther. It seems unlikely that anyone will have a problem, and it is easy to monkey-patch if they do. 

It's time to be pedantically correct. :smile: 



Footnotes:

[1] This is something that can be done with colorimetry and color perception models. I can send slides if you are curious.

[2] POV-Ray is older than the sRGB standard and the gamma curve settings can let simulate various media or raw light intensities. 

[3] I made this comparison: ![old_vs_new_styles_2M](/uploads/d55419788c44e984fe739abd8fb7dcfa/old_vs_new_styles_2M.jpg){width=208 height=600}

[4] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRGB

[5] ![ase_color_rendering_improvements_on_the_ASE_website](/uploads/47001a90ac21efcebc4dd1a1d8d65f87/ase_color_rendering_improvements_on_the_ASE_website.png){width=848 height=600}

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @mwalter for the update! The change looks reasonable, and the failure of the `lint` pipeline is not related to the present MR. I think we can merge very soon. Just to trace back the historical development, may I ask a question? There have been back-and-forth changes in !2767 and !2772. Is the following my understanding correct?

- [Since POV-Ray 3.7.0 (released on 2013-11-06), the `sRGB` option is available for `Display_gamma`.](https://www.povray.org/download/)
- https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/merge_requests/2767 addresses this change.
- Soon a backward-compatibility issue raised up due to the ASE test environment at the time (used POV-Ray 3.6.1), and therefore once reverted back to `2.2` as workaround.
- [Later the ASE test environment has been updated](https://gitlab.com/ase/ase-dockers/-/blob/master/debian-calculators/Dockerfile#L9), where [POV-Ray 3.7.0 is already available](https://packages.debian.org/trixie/povray). So, the present MR sets `sRGB` again.

thread.actionability_reasoning: This is a historical/contextual question seeking to confirm understanding of past changes, with no suggestion of a code change. The comment also notes the lint failure is unrelated and expresses readiness to merge.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Thank you so much @mjwaters for the detailed information! I agree that setting `Display_gamma` explicitly makes the figure substantially more beautiful and also agree that following the standard is nice. Let's merge :)

thread.actionability_reasoning: Pure acknowledgment and approval to merge, with no code change suggestions.
